import { gzipSync } from 'node:zlib';

  .filter(([path]) => !path.includes('node_modules/'))
  .reduce((sum, [, info]) => sum + info.bytesInOutput, 0);
console.log(file, gzipSync(r.outputFiles[0].contents, { level: 9 }).byteLength, 'bytes (min+gzip),', own, 'bytes of own code');

The migrated file is written to `out/module.ts`. Type checking passes, but I couldn't compare it with the original, because lodash isn't installed here and the original `src/module.ts` fails to build. It bundles at 2280 bytes min+gzip, with 85 bytes of my own code.

The imports are now:
- **`merge`** comes from `es-toolkit/object`. Arrays merge by index and `null` overwrites a value, as in lodash. For example, `{a:[1,2,3]}` patched with `{a:[9]}` gives `{a:[9,2,3]}`.
- **`startCase` and `isEmpty`** come from `es-toolkit/compat`.

I chose compat for `startCase` on purpose. The main `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, so `API` would become `Api`, and your input range includes consecutive capitals. The compat version keeps capitals the way lodash does. On the examples it gives `Width 91 Api Width` and `Apiurl Api 0 36`.

The main entry has no `isEmpty`, only `isEmptyObject`, so compat is the only option there too.

I only spot-checked the outputs by hand. The one gap I know of is an input object that has a numeric `length` key. Compat `isEmpty` may treat it differently from lodash, and I didn't test it.
